stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Targeted code guidelines</span></h2><span data-as="p">Code Guidelines previously applied only to the directory tree containing the guideline file, which meant guideline documents had to mirror your source layout to cover the right code. Teams can now decouple the two with a <code>filePatterns</code> object entry: <code>files</code> locates the guideline document and <code>applyTo</code> defines the source-file pattern it governs, so a guideline stored anywhere in the repository (for example in a shared <code>docs/</code> folder) can apply to any matching files, regardless of where they live.</span><span data-as="p">The existing string form remains fully supported with its directory-scoped behavior and requires no migration.</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/knowledge-base/code-guidelines">Code Guidelines documentation</a> for details.</span></div></div></div>

Define <strong>Post-Merge Actions</strong> as natural-language instructions. For example, append a changelog entry, file a Linear or Jira ticket, open a GitHub issue, or post a Slack summary. CodeRabbit executes them agentically against the merged changes.</span><span data-as="p">Each enabled action is previewed as a checkbox in the <strong>🚀 Post-Merge Actions</strong> section of the PR walkthrough, checked when CodeRabbit judges it applicable to the change. The author or a reviewer can skip all actions, or named actions, with <code>@coderabbitai skip post-merge actions</code> (optionally <code>--name &quot;...&quot;</code>) before merging. On merge into the default branch, CodeRabbit runs the still-checked actions and posts a single result comment. Code-changing actions land as a follow-up pull request.</span><span data-as="p">Configure up to five actions per organization from <strong>Settings → Post-merge actions</strong> or in <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code> under <code>reviews.post_merge_actions</code>. See the <a class="link" href="/pr-reviews/post-merge-actions">Post-Merge Actions documentation</a> for details.</span></div></div></div>

linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">CLI v0.6.5 </span></h2><span data-as="p">v0.6.5 improves sign-in, local review summaries, and reliability for updates and long-running review sessions.</span><ul>
<li>SSO sign-in now handles multi-provider workspaces more clearly, preserves the CLI callback through organization selection, and resolves the right workspace organization for enterprise SSO users.</li>
<li>Local reviews now preserve real <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code> diffs when that file is also loaded as configuration, and the completion summary shows which files CodeRabbit reviewed.</li>
<li>Review diffs now prefer remote-tracking base branches when local branches are stale, reducing false too-many-files skips.</li>
<li>Attempts with no reviewable hunks no longer consume review quota.</li>
<li>Review sessions and self-updates clean up more reliably: the CLI opens review WebSockets only when it is ready to submit, idle connections close after terminal events, and staged update files are removed from temp storage.</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/cli/index">CLI documentation</a> and <a class="link" href="/cli/reference">CLI Command Reference</a> for more details.</span></div></div></div>

<strong>Quiet</strong> review profile alongside the existing <strong>Chill</strong> and <strong>Assertive</strong> profiles. Set it with <code>reviews.profile: quiet</code> in your <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code>, or choose it from your repository settings.</span><span data-as="p">Quiet keeps your pull request conversation focused: only the most important comments — critical and major issues that are also high-impact — are posted inline. Every other comment is grouped into collapsed sections in the review summary, so nothing is lost while the inline noise stays low.</span><span data-as="p">The three profiles now range from least to most feedback: <code>quiet</code> for only the most important feedback, <code>chill</code> for balanced feedback (the default), and <code>assertive</code> for more comprehensive feedback (which may feel nitpicky).</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/reference/configuration">configuration reference</a> and the <a class="link" href="/reference/glossary#profile">Profile glossary entry</a> for details.</span></div></div></div>

linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">CLI v0.6.0 </span></h2><span data-as="p">v0.6.0 makes local reviews faster to start, easier to understand, and simpler to operate.</span><ul>
<li><code>coderabbit review --fast</code> adds an explicit opt-in for faster local reviews.</li>
<li>Auth status, sign-in, organization selection, and rate-limit messages now provide clearer context in <code>coderabbit auth status</code>.</li>
<li><code>--interactive</code> and <code>--prompt-only</code> are deprecated; use plain review mode and <code>coderabbit review --agent</code>.</li>
<li>Ctrl-C now exits review and auth cleanup promptly.</li>
<li>Repository-to-organization matching now handles SSH remotes with non-<code>git</code> users (such as GitHub Enterprise org-named users), <code>ssh://</code> remotes with custom ports, and self-hosted instances registered on custom web ports or subpaths, so reviews attribute to your installed organization instead of falling back to free review limits.</li>
<li>Branch lists are no longer corrupted by Git worktree markers when a branch is checked out in another worktree.</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/cli/index">CLI documentation</a> and <a class="link" href="/cli/reference">CLI Command Reference</a> for more details.</span></div></div></div>

Enable it with <code>knowledge_base.automatic_repository_linking: true</code> in <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code>, or from <strong>Knowledge Base</strong> &gt; <strong>Linked Repositories</strong> in the app.</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/knowledge-base/multi-repo-analysis#automatic-repository-linking">Automatic Repository Linking documentation</a> for details.</span></div></div></div>

and makes agent-mode pipelines more reliable.</span><ul>
<li>Plain-text output now includes a finding count and per-severity breakdown at the end of each run; individual finding cards are easier to scan mid-output.</li>
<li><code>coderabbit review findings</code> replays locally cached results from the last run. <code>coderabbit review --show-prompts</code> prints the AI prompts used in that run.</li>
<li>Agent mode now emits <code>heartbeat</code> events during long reviews, includes a <code>comment</code> field as a fallback when <code>codegenInstructions</code> is absent, and warns when plain mode is used inside a detected agent environment.</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/cli/index">CLI documentation</a> and <a class="link" href="/cli/reference">CLI Command Reference</a> for more details.</span></div></div></div>

class="cursor-pointer">CodeRabbit Change Stack</span></h2><span data-as="p"> | <!-- --> </span><span data-as="p">Change Stack is a new <strong>code review interface</strong> that reorganizes a pull request from a flat file list into a guided, layer-by-layer walkthrough, so reviewers can follow the change in the logical, explorable order, not in alphabetical file order.</span><span data-as="p">AI-authored PRs tend to be larger and touch more files than handwritten ones: main changes, new migrations, consumers, call sites, and tests all in one diff. GitHub surfaces these as a flat file list, leaving reviewers to reconstruct the meaning themselves before they can evaluate anything. Change Stack is designed to assist with the review of larger, harder-to-read AI-written changes.</span><span data-as="p">Change Stack organizes a PR into ordered <strong>cohorts</strong> and <strong>layers</strong> anchored to specific line ranges, each with its own <strong>range-specific summary</strong>. Diagrams are generated inline where they add value: sequence diagrams for new call flows, ERDs for data model changes.</span><div><figure data-name="frame" class="frame p-2 not-prose relative top-level message in their home channel, not just on a recurring schedule. Use message-triggered automations when you want CodeRabbit to react to messages in Slack, such as Datadog alerts, deployment notices, or queue-health posts. You can:</span><ul>
<li>Match every new top-level message in the channel</li>
<li>Restrict runs to messages whose text includes specific case-insensitive substrings</li>
<li>Restrict runs to specific Slack bots or Slack apps with a required author allowlist</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">Message-triggered automations always reply in the triggering thread. <code>Run now</code> is not available for this trigger type; post a matching bot or app message in the channel to test it.</span></div></div></div>

feature branches, a rapid stream of small commits can trigger a new incremental review after every push, most reviewing near-identical diffs. To avoid noisy feedback, CodeRabbit now automatically pauses incremental reviews after <strong>5 reviewed commits</strong> on a pull request (default). After the limit is reached, use <code>@coderabbitai review</code> to request a fresh review on demand.</span><span data-as="p">You can set the desired commit count with <code>auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits</code> in <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code> or under <strong>Reviews</strong> in your repository or organization settings, or set it to <code>0</code> to disable the pause entirely and always review every push.</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/configuration/auto-review#auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits">automatic review controls</a> for details.</span></div></div></div>

billing practices.</span><span data-as="p"><strong>How it works:</strong></span><ul>
<li><strong>Delayed unassignment</strong>: When you unassign a seat from a monthly subscriber, it remains active until the end of your current billing cycle</li>
<li><strong>Continued access</strong>: Users with “Pending unassignment” seats retain full CodeRabbit access until the billing cycle ends</li>
<li><strong>Automatic cleanup</strong>: At the end of the billing cycle, “Pending unassignment” seats are automatically unassigned</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">“Pending unassignment” seats are still counted as active seats for billing purposes during the current cycle. This approach ensures you get full value from your subscription while giving you the flexibility to adjust your team composition as needed.</span><span data-as="p">Note: This “Pending unassignment” behavior applies only to monthly paid subscriptions. Annual subscriptions are not affected.</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/management/seat-assignment#pending-unassignment">Pending unassignment documentation</a> for more details.</span></div></div></div>

inheritance</span></h2><span data-as="p">You can now enable configuration inheritance to share common settings across repositories while allowing individual customizations. When enabled, CodeRabbit merges configuration from parent levels for values not explicitly defined at the current level.</span><span data-as="p"><strong>What’s new:</strong></span><ul>
<li><strong>Opt-in inheritance</strong> - Enable with <code>inheritance: true</code> in your repository <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code> configuration file</li>
<li><strong>Smart merge behavior</strong> - When your repository doesn’t define a setting, it inherits from parent levels; nested settings combine, lists merge without duplicates, and scalars override defaults</li>
<li><strong>Hierarchical configuration</strong> - Merge across repository, central, organization, and default levels</li>
<li><strong>Flexible control</strong> - Stop inheritance chain at any level with <code>inheritance: false</code></li>
</ul><span data-as="p">Common use cases include setting organization-wide defaults while allowing repository-specific overrides, and creating team-specific configurations that build on parent settings.</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/configuration/configuration-inheritance">configuration inheritance documentation</a> for setup instructions and examples.</span></div></div></div>

interface</span></h2><span data-as="p">The web interface now supports both UI and YAML editing modes for organization and repository settings.</span><span aria-owns="rmiz-modal-" data-rmiz=""><span data-rmiz-content="not-found" style="visibility:visible"><picture class="contents"><img data-path="images/changelog/yaml-ui-config-switch.gif" src="https://mintcdn.com/coderabbit/ypIuAyTjC1akBz54/images/changelog/yaml-ui-config-switch.gif?s=ff6f492454c6702053fd46fe4fd07a43" alt="YAML and UI config switching" class="object-contain" width="1584" height="1080" decoding="async" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" data-optimize="true" style="aspect-ratio:1584 / 1080"/></picture></span></span><span data-as="p"><strong>What’s new:</strong></span><ul>
<li><strong>UI Mode (default)</strong> - Interactive form with dropdowns, checkboxes, and input fields for guided configuration</li>
<li><strong>YAML Mode</strong> - Direct YAML editing with syntax highlighting and real-time validation for advanced users</li>
<li><strong>Easily switch between modes</strong> - Use the <strong>Edit YAML</strong> button to switch between modes (changes to <strong>Return to UI</strong> when in YAML mode)</li>
<li><strong>Real-time sync</strong> - Changes made in either mode are immediately reflected when switching between them</li>
<li><strong>Clean YAML output</strong> - Only non-default values are displayed in YAML mode for cleaner configuration</li>
<li><strong>Clipboard support</strong> - Copy the entire YAML configuration to your clipboard for easy transfer to <code>.coderabbit.yaml</code> files</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">This enhancement makes it easier to manage settings whether you prefer visual forms or direct YAML editing, and ensures consistency between web interface and repository-based configurations.</span><span data-as="p">See the <a class="link" href="/guides/organization-settings">organization settings documentation</a> and <a class="link" href="/guides/repository-settings">repository settings documentation</a> for more details.</span></div></div></div>

<li>📝 <strong>Inline Code Reviews</strong>: Senior-dev-level annotation on every line. CodeRabbit becomes your AI pair programmer, annotating staged &amp; unstaged commits before you even open a PR.</li>
<li>🚀 <strong>Built for Flow, Not Friction</strong>: Code, review, commit—rise &amp; repeat without breaking your flow state. Reviews run automatically on every commit so you ship faster.</li>
<li>🛠️ <strong>Fix-with-AI</strong>: One-Click Fix for quick tweaks; “Fix with AI” hands off more complex suggestions to your favorite coding agent, complete with full context.</li>
<li>🧩 <strong>Compatible with Cursor, Windsurf &amp; Language-Agnostic</strong>: Works out of the box on VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf. Supports Java, JavaScript, PHP, Python, TypeScript, Go, Ruby, and more.</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">Pair these IDE-embedded reviews with our deeper Git-platform reviews for a multi-layered approach that catches more bugs and cuts down overall review time.</span><ul>

<li>CodeRabbit now automatically detects Semgrep rulesets from default <code>semgrep.yml</code> or <code>semgrep.config.yml</code> files, eliminating the need for manual configuration.</li>

<li><strong>Gitleaks</strong>: A lightweight, open-source secret scanner to prevent security breaches</li>

With this improvement, we now stop the review process midway if we detect that the PR has been closed.</span></div></div></div>

recursive autonomous agent, CodeRabbit uses shell scripts to perform complex operations on the entire codebase, verifying changes and providing deeper insights.</span><span data-as="p">Here are some use cases:</span><ul>
<li>Want to defer implementing the CodeRabbit suggestion to a later time? Ask the bot to create an issue</li>
<li>Generate unit tests - comment <code>@coderabbitai generate unit tests</code> for the src/utils.ts</li>
<li>In PR comments, ask the bot to gather insights on your repository including latest commits, frequently changed files, recent contributors etc</li>
<li>When the CodeRabbit review comment is addressed, let the bot know and it can validate with the latest commit</li>
</ul><span data-as="p">Really excited to see how this feature gets used, especially with access to the CLI commands. There are some suggestions in the pull request tips but we are looking forward to seeing additional use cases of how developers use this feature.
